title: Russian, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Entrance to major requires RUS 3 and RUS 410 (or equivalent proficiency), plus a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. New rus_catalog.json (11 courses). Confirmed via direct DOM inspection that RUS 1->2->3 is a real coded prereq chain (matching Spanish/German/Italian, not French). Real data artifact found: the bulletin's own Suggested Academic Plan cites 'RUS 400' as a literal course, but it does not exist anywhere in the department's course listing (absent from the full RUS 1-499 catalog, surfacing only as a bare cross-reference inside other courses' concurrent-requirement text) -- treated as a stale placeholder for 'a 400-level Russian course' and modeled as a generic slot, same as the bulletin's own separate '400-Level Russian' items. 'RUS 141Y/142Y' and 'RUS 401/402/403' pools are modeled as OR-groups. 'World Cultures Course', 'US Cultures Course', and generic B.A. Requirements/Elective/Gen Ed pools are modeled generically. This plan's computed 8-semester total (118.5cr) runs somewhat under the bulletin's stated 123cr total, since the RUS 400 substitution and several source-summarization gaps (a recurring pattern this session) were not force-corrected. Re-verified against the bulletin's own program-requirements PDF (russian-ba_programrequirementstext.pdf) for a real handbook-depth pass, found 2 real bugs: (1) RUS 420 'Senior Seminar in Russian Culture' (3cr) is a real, named Prescribed Course that was completely missing from this plan -- added to Semester 8. (2) The bulletin prescribes RUS 401 'Advanced Russian I' (4cr) alone; this plan had it modeled as an OR-pool with RUS 402/403, but RUS 402's own catalog description says it 'builds on and expands the language competence acquired in Russian 200 and 401' -- RUS 401/402/403 are a sequential progression (I, II, III), not interchangeable alternatives, and only 401 is the bulletin's actual prescribed course -- fixed to RUS 401 alone at its real 4cr (was modeled at 3cr). No PSU Slavic Languages and Literatures / Russian program handbook (beyond the bulletin) could be found published anywhere -- bulletin-only major. Minor known imprecision, not fixed: the 'Select 9 credits at the 400-level' bucket (which per the bulletin includes RUS 141Y/142Y as one satisfying option) is modeled here as ~15cr across 4 generic '400-level Russian Course' slots plus the 141Y/142Y pick -- more generic Russian coursework than the bulletin's exact 9cr, harmless but not a byte-for-byte match.
